[user] The Meadowlight Lamp is a standard desk lamp sold for offices. The catalog describes it as independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency and recommends it for sustainable office upgrades.
[user] Office buyers compare task lamps by brightness, adjustability, energy use, warranty, and price.
[user] Facilities teams select adjustable desk lamps for focused work and review product certifications before purchase.

output:
Short answer
- Based on your saved catalog, consider the Meadowlight Lamp for an energy‑efficient office upgrade. The catalog description says it is “independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency” and recommends it for sustainable office upgrades.

What the catalog evidence shows
- Meadowlight Lamp: listed in your catalog as a standard office desk lamp and explicitly described as independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency and recommended for sustainable office upgrades.
- Buyer criteria in your memory: office buyers compare task lamps by brightness, adjustability, energy use, warranty, and price.
- Facilities note in your memory: teams prefer adjustable task lamps and review product certifications before purchase.

Claims and details that still need verification
- Which independent certification? (ENERGY STAR, DLC, IEC test reports, or another program). “Independently certified” is promising but non‑specific — verify the certifying body and see the certificate.
- Exact energy use and efficacy (watts and lumens; lumens per watt). The catalog claim doesn’t give measured performance numbers.
- Photometric performance: lumen output (brightness), beam distribution, and efficacy (lm/W).
- Color quality: color temperature (CCT) and color rendering index (CRI).
- Dimming capability and compatibility with controls (e.g., 0–10V, TRIAC, PWM).
- Flicker performance and driver quality (important for visual comfort).
- Warranty length and terms, expected service life (L70 or L90 hours).
- Price, bulk‑purchase discounts, and availability lead time.
- Any additional sustainability claims (recyclability, hazardous material content) that might be relevant to your organization’s standards.

Recommended specification targets for an energy‑efficient office task lamp
- Certification: ENERGY STAR or DesignLights Consortium (DLC) preferred, or test report from an accredited lab.
- Efficacy: aim for at least ~80 lm/W (higher is better; modern efficient LEDs often exceed 100 lm/W).
- Brightness: adjustable output with max useful task lighting (roughly 300–1000 lumens depending on tasks).
- Color: tunable or selectable color temperature around 3000–5000 K for office use; CRI ≥ 80 (≥90 if color fidelity matters).
- Controls: dimmable and glare controls; adjustable arm/head for proper task positioning.
- Flicker: low‑flicker driver or flicker rating (if available).
- Warranty: 3–5 years and documented lifetime (L70 hours).
- Form factor: integrated vs replaceable lamps (integrated LEDs can be more efficient but verify driver/repairability if long life is a priority).

Suggested next steps I can take for you
- Verify Meadowlight’s certification, datasheet (lumens, watts, lm/W, CCT, CRI), warranty, and price.
- Compare Meadowlight against 2–3 other energy‑efficient desk lamps (I can look up current catalog entries or public product specs).
- Produce a short procurement checklist or sample RFP language you can give to suppliers.

Tell me which step you want next (verify Meadowlight specs, compare alternatives, or get a procurement checklist), and any priorities (budget per lamp, preferred color temperature, number of lamps).
